# Container runbook

This directory packages the reviewer workbench, the existing single-shot review
service and the repository checks into containers. It adds no review, calculation
or approval behavior: each container runs the repository's own entry points.

**Synthetic only.** Every input is generated by the repository's own fixture
launchers inside disposable volumes. Nothing here is production login, business
approval or AWS acceptance, and a passing container run is not evidence of
real-case accuracy. Published ports bind to loopback; do not expose them.

## The workbench

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:4174 and sign in with the token the launcher issued:

```bash
docker compose exec workbench workbench-entrypoint fixture
```

That prints the private manifest: `session_token`, `empty_job_id`,
`completed_job_id` and the five response task IDs. It is local authentication
configuration, not a publishable report — keep it out of Git and out of evidence.

### Why one container

`scripts/run_local_workbench.py` binds uvicorn to `127.0.0.1` with no host option,
and `create_integrated_service` refuses any request whose `Host` is not its own
numeric loopback authority. Both are deliberate. So the frontend and the API share
a container: nginx serves the built frontend on 8080 and proxies `/v1/` to
`127.0.0.1:8765`, presenting that authority verbatim. Only the frontend origin is
published. The API is not reachable from the Docker network or the host.

The frontend is built with `VITE_API_BASE_URL` unset, which is what makes the
same-origin `/v1/` routes correct. Client-side routes (`/jobs/:id`, `/tasks/:id`)
fall back to the app shell.

### What works and what does not

Working in this container: sign-in with an issued token, job status, durable
result, findings and verification, human tasks with their citations, task
responses, and authenticated PDF download verified against the manifest digest.

Not in this container: the `/privacy` route. It needs a separate local bridge plus
an operator-owned Tesseract executable and language assets pinned by SHA-256, which
must be selected on the host and never baked into an image. Use
`scripts/run_integration_rehearsal.py` from the
[integrated local runbook](../docs/integrated-local-runbook.md) for that.

State lives in the `workbench` volume. Mutation scenarios consume tasks, so the
entrypoint reopens durable state rather than resetting it. To repeat every browser
scenario from the start, take a new volume with `docker compose down -v`.

## The single-shot review demo

The earlier deterministic surface is kept behind a profile:

```bash
docker compose --profile review-demo up --build
```

| Surface | Address | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Console | http://127.0.0.1:8080 | Visual pipeline view over the reference service |
| Reviewer | http://127.0.0.1:8000 | `/health`, `/v1/validate`, `/v1/reviews` |
| Reviewer (gate) | http://127.0.0.1:8001 | The same service pinned to material missing evidence |

It runs three scenarios against the real endpoints — review only, review and write
the PDF, and a blocked run whose evidence is missing — and shows the HTTP call,
workflow and artifact status, verification, audit events, the independent factor
calculation, findings with their source excerpt, page and bounding box, coverage,
the artifact and the unmodified response body. A cited region can be drawn over a
render of its own source page, limited to documents the input manifest allowlists
and still hash-matches.

The workbench above supersedes this for demonstration purposes; it is retained
because it exercises the reference service directly and shows the completion gate
side by side.

## Checks

```bash
docker compose --profile verify run --rm verify      # Python
docker compose --profile verify run --rm web-verify  # frontend
```

`verify` runs Ruff, `ruff format --check`, mypy, pytest with coverage, the reviewed
full-case goldens, `cloud_tests`, the synthetic API HTTP smoke, the local service
smoke and `cfn-lint`, reporting every step rather than stopping at the first
failure, and exits non-zero if any failed. It installs Git because the
publication-gate tests drive real repositories. `scripts/check_submission.py
--base origin/main` needs this checkout's history, which the image does not carry;
run that one on the host.

`web-verify` runs the frontend's own `npm run verify`: typecheck, lint, format
check, unit tests, build and artifact checks. Playwright browser smoke is separate
and is not run here.

Both images resolve their dependency ranges fresh, so a step can fail here while
the same step passes against an older pinned environment on the host. That
difference is the point: it is what a clean install sees.

## Image layout

`deploy/Dockerfile`, on `python:3.12-slim` and `node:22-bookworm-slim`, matching
the runtime versions the integrated local runbook requires. Python stages run as
UID 10001 with a real passwd entry, because the local approval store binds receipts
to an OS account.

- `webbuild` — `npm ci` and `npm run build` for `web/`.
- `base` — the package with the `aws`, `pdf`, `documents` and `privacy` extras.
- `workbench` — adds nginx, the launcher and the built frontend.
- `reviewer` — the reference service and its fixture entrypoint.
- `console` — the demo console over that service.
- `verify` / `web-verify` — the two check suites.

These images are a local rehearsal. They are not a deployment target, carry no
hosted identity, and do not replace the AWS work in
[the architecture](../docs/architecture.md).
